name: figma-cursor

frames.best_why: All three labelled cursors are spread apart and legible over both mock frames at once.

tagline: Coloured name tags with pointer arrows drift around a shared canvas.
summary: Three labelled cursors in blue, pink and green move slowly along looping paths over a mock design. Each pill carries a name and an arrow, like collaborators in a shared editing tool.
appearance: Three rounded name pills in blue, pink and green, each paired with a small matching pointer arrow, floating over a dark canvas that holds two outlined mock frames.
behaviour: Each pill and arrow drifts along its own short looping path, moving right and down then back again. The motion repeats forever on timers of roughly four to five seconds.
demo_content: 'Frame 12 · Pricing' and 'Frame 14 · Checkout' cards; names Maya Chen, Leo Park, Ana Ruiz.
use_when: A demo needs to suggest live collaborators or multiplayer presence on a shared canvas.
avoid_when: It is decorative only; the cursors are fake and follow no real pointer or user.
customise: Pass text plus optional colour, stroke, pixel offsets, duration and delay. Path shape and the endless loop are fixed in the source.
weight_why: Three small pills and arrows moved by transform on a repeat timer; cheap to run.

a11y.note: Decorative motion with no control; it ignores reduced-motion and keeps looping for everyone.

issues: The drift loop never pauses and does not respect reduced-motion settings.
The cursors are purely fake and never follow the real pointer.
polish_why: Clean coloured pills and smooth drift, but it is a familiar idea implemented plainly.
